title: Qcqs lisse rational modules have stratified integral lattices
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$, the condensed ring of continuous functions to normed $E$, or $\Lambda=\Omega^{\mathrm{fin}}$, whose sections on a profinite set are continuous functions to $\Omega$ with image in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\mathcal F=\{E\}$ in the first case and let $\mathcal F$ be all finite subextensions of $\Omega$ in the second. For $F\in\mathcal F$ write $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ with its norm topology. For each scheme $T$, use the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T,F_T,A_{F,T}$ on the small pro-étale site, module objects, and ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Constructibility means finite constant scalar models on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; $D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ means bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A lisse module is pro-étale locally free of finite rank. A scheme is qcqs when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

Let $T$ be qcqs and $M$ a lisse $\Lambda_T$-module. There exist $F\in\mathcal F$, a lisse $F_T$-module $L$, an isomorphism $\Lambda_T\otimes_{F_T}L\cong M$, and a finite partition $T=\coprod_s S_s$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], such that each $L|_{S_s}$ contains a lisse $A_{F,S_s}$-submodule $B_s$ whose inclusion induces an isomorphism $F_{S_s}\otimes_{A_{F,S_s}}B_s\cong L|_{S_s}$. Thus the induced map $\Lambda_{S_s}\otimes_{A_{F,S_s}}B_s\to M|_{S_s}$ is an isomorphism. In the finite-extension case one can take $F=E$, $L=M$ and the identity for the first isomorphism. Rank zero, empty schemes, and varying ranks are allowed. There is no Noetherian, dimension, characteristic or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis.

proof.text: Convert IsLisseCoefficientModule to the raw-cover LocallyFree predicate: on the same cover, extension along the invertible condensedPullbackHom preserves and reflects finite free modules. For algebraic-closure coefficients apply exists_lisse_finiteCoefficient_model once on the qcqs base. For finite coefficients retain the original module and field.

For the fixed finite field and every point x, apply continuousLisse_affine_etale_lattice to obtain an affine etale neighbourhood carrying an integral locally free module whose scalar extension is the rational pullback. The neighbourhood images are open and cover X. Compactness selects a finite subfamily. Apply the finite-coproduct lattice construction and the finite-affine cover geometry helper of ContinuousEtaleLocalLattices: the scheme coproduct is affine, hence qcqs, and its map to X is etale and surjective. This argument uses only compactness, not Noetherianity, and includes an empty finite family and varying ranks.

Apply exists_etale_stratified_finite to this qcqs etale cover and retain its constructible strata. On each stratum put q = pullback.snd p j and r = pullback.fst p j. The map q is finite etale by that theorem and surjective by stability of scheme surjectivity under base change. Pull the integral module along r and the rational module along j; locallyFree_upperStar preserves their local freeness. Compose pullIso with the pulled original scalar-extension comparison, upperStarComp, the actual pullback.condition, and upperStarComp again. This gives the precise isomorphism E tensor r* M ≅ q* j* P.

Apply continuousFiniteEtaleTrace_lattice to q and this comparison to obtain an epic trace whose actual integral image is locally free. Let F be integral scalar extension and g the composite of the pushed lattice embedding and restricted trace. The underived push comparison and the localization counit make F of the pushed embedding invertible. Naturality of the counit identifies F(g) followed by the counit with that invertible map followed by trace, hence F(g) is epic. The image factorization implies F of the image inclusion is epic. Exactness makes it monic, hence invertible. Composing with the invertible counit gives the adjoint image inclusion. Rewrite the scalar adjunction through mkOfHomEquiv_homEquiv to identify this adjoint with Mod.extendHom. The normed finite-subfield integral coefficient ring and its inclusion agree definitionally with padicIntegersRingObj and padicIntegersToPadicSubfield. Convert raw-cover local freeness back to IsLisseCoefficientModule, giving the finite-field assertion. Package lattice existence as a property of the coefficient diagram; generic proved packing/unpacking transports the normed-field theorem along the definitional equality of its coefficient diagram with the finite-subfield diagram, keeping all actual inclusions and rationalization maps.

Apply the finite-field assertion to the finite model in the algebraic-closure case. Retain the same strata, lattices and monic inclusions. The displayed final morphism is a composite of the scalar-extension associator, the extension of the invertible lattice rationalization, the invertible coefficient/pullback comparison, and the pullback of the finite-model comparison. Each factor is invertible, so their composite is invertible. This is precisely the displayed composite in the existing theorem; its signature is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Etale local lattice existence, finite affine subcover by compactness, constructible finite-etale stratification (Stacks 03S0), trace-image descent, and finite coefficient model. Reuses existing affine and finite-coproduct lattice declarations rather than constructing a separate rank partition and representing scheme.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 needs descent of a lisse object for the finite-subextension-valued coefficient on qcqs schemes; the compactification unit does not give coefficient descent.
Step 2 needs finite clopen rank loci for a lisse finite-field module on a quasi-compact scheme.
Step 3 needs the separated étale representing lattice scheme and its universal embedded lattice on a qcqs base.
Step 3 refines the lattice-scheme covering to a finite affine étale cover without assuming its source quasi-compact.
Step 3 uses finite coproducts of affine pro-étale objects and their qcqs underlying schemes.
Steps 3 and 4 preserve lisse modules on base changes; no such coefficient pullback statement is supplied by the compactification unit.
Steps 3 and 4 use exact underlying coefficient pullback, preserving embedded lattices and their scalar extensions.
Step 4 uses exactly the qcqs stratification of an étale morphism in Stacks Tag 03S0, rather than imposing Noetherianity.
Steps 5 and 6 identify embedded internal lattices and their rationalizations with the continuous-function coefficient encoding.
Step 5 uses the globally defined trace image and its local equality with a sum of sheet submodules.
Step 5 uses finite étale local splitting, valid for arbitrary schemes.
Step 6 makes finitely many lattices simultaneously constant after a local refinement of a free rational module.
Step 6 uses the full sheaf-sum assertion, its local freeness and the rationalization of its inclusion.

Steps 4 and 7 carry the rationalization isomorphism and the scalar-extension isomorphism alpha along the locally closed immersions; inverse image commuting with internal extension of scalars is not given by the compactification unit (citation added by the maintainer reader).
